Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
300 AM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Dry/continental air related to high pressure that will build 
  across and offshore the Middle Atlantic will favor lower surface 
  dewpoints/afternoon RH and low temperatures, both of which have 
  been adjusted lower by several degrees than the NBM/official 
  forecast, through Wed.
  

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 300 AM Monday...

1) Seasonable start to the second week of September

2) Above normal temperatures return by mid week, with increasing 
shower/storm chances Thursday and Friday

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 300 AM Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Seasonable start to the second week of 
September

A lower mid-latidue/subtropical ridge over the srn Plains will 
progress ewd and reach the Carolinas by 12Z Wed. Rising heights and 
weakening nwly flow aloft will result over cntl NC. 

Beneath and downstream of the ridge aloft, 1022 mb surface high 
pressure will build across and offshore the Middle Atlantic, while 
extending wwd into NC. Influence from the ridge and associated 
continental/dry air will favor mixed/afternoon surface dewpoints in 
the 50s, except lwr 60s in the Coastal Plain and ern Sandhills and 
also low temperatures in the 50s to lwr 60s. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... Above normal temperatures return by mid week, with 
increasing shower/storm chances Thursday and Friday

Strong ridging will remain in place across much of the southern US 
through mid week, with H5 heights forecast to steadily increase 
across NC through Wednesday (peaking around 594-596dm). Meanwhile at 
the surface, a 1025mb ridge off the Mid Atlantic coast will support 
increasing southerly flow area-wide. While dewpoints will be slow to 
recover and remain in the low to mid 60s on Wednesday, they will 
climb markedly Thursday into Friday with upper 60s to lower 70s 
becoming increasingly common. This will translate into steadily 
increasing heat index values reaching the mid 90s Thursday and 
Friday. 

As the upper ridge continues to flatten, we'll eventually see a 
longwave trough and attendant surface cold front move out of the 
Ohio Valley and into the Mid Atlantic/Southeast late in the week. As 
such we'll see increasing shower and storm chances as early as 
Thursday afternoon within an increasingly unstable pre-frontal 
airmass. There is still some uncertainty with respect to when the 
front/trough will move through NC (most ensemble guidance suggests 
Friday vs Thursday night), but we'll continue to maintain increased 
PoPs through the day Friday given ensemble support. That said the 
strongest forcing for ascent associated with the trough should be 
displaced well north of NC and it remains to be seen just how much 
QPF is realized with the front when it arrives. 

Precip chances should decrease in the wake of the front through the 
weekend. Temps will also decrease, albeit slightly, with highs 
reaching the upper 80s/lower 90s Saturday and Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
As of 130 AM Monday...

Nely flow around high pressure building across the Great Lakes and 
Middle Atlantic will become gusty into the teens kts with daytime 
heating primarily at FAY, and more briefly at RWI and RDU around 
midday. 

Outlook: High pressure over the Middle Atlantic will favor VFR 
conditions through mid week, with the exception of a chance of 
shallow, radiation fog/mist at RWI due to local effects. A frontal 
zone will settle into the NC with a chance of convection and 
associated flight restrictions on Fri. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...
A couple of strong shortwaves the past couple of days have
worked over the east/west heat dome/ridge and its arguable we
could be in a cyclonic flow aloft. Any convection today should
be pushed well to the south if it affects our area at all. More
noticeable will be highs in the middle to upper 80s and lows
except right along the coast in the 60s.

&&

.AVIATION /09Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
High confidence in mainly VFR conditions for the 12Z TAF period. 
Just a very low risk of brief restrictions from low clouds early
this AM and showers/storms just about anytime, especially near the
coast. Otherwise, breezy NE winds will prevail today, especially
near the coast. 

Extended Outlook... Mostly VFR conditions as drier high 
pressure builds in from the north.

&&

.MARINE...
A decent NE flow will develop today enough to warrant a
marginal smalll craft advisory through tonight. For the mid week
period winds will diminish and take on a more easterly flow.
Signigicant seas will be 3-5 with the headline diminishing to
2-4 feet.

&&

FXUS62 KJAX 070609
AFDJAX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
209 AM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- Localized Flooding Rain Risk Today

- Moderate Rip Current Risk Today - High Risk Wednesday

- Daily Afternoon & Evening Thunderstorms 

&&

.NEAR TERM /THROUGH TONIGHT/...
Highlights Through Tonight:

- Unsettled Weather & Cooler Today

- Localized Flood Risk Continues

Cloudy and cooler today with waves of showers and storms as a 
surface front across the Carolinas early this morning settles 
farther south and extends across north FL or very near the GA-FL 
state line by this afternoon. The mid-level trough across the region 
will edge slightly farther south today with the axis across north 
Florida. This will bring slightly drier air (PWATs falling below 2 
inches under northerly flow) across southeast GA into the afternoon 
while keeping richer moisture and stronger lift across northeast FL, 
near and south of the surface front. Higher rain chances this 
morning will focus across northeast FL and along the Atlantic coast 
where onshore, breezy northeast winds develop on the northern side 
of the surface front. Into the afternoon, rain chances expand east 
to west as diurnal instability increases and another vorticity max 
within the mid level trough pivots southward across north-central 
FL. Breezy northeast winds develop north of the front along the 
southeast GA coast this morning, then east-northeast winds expand 
southward through the afternoon as the surface front settles farther 
south of north Florida as high pressure strengthens northeast of the 
region. An inverted coastal trough begins to form tonight over the 
adjacent coastal waters, with elevated northeast winds along the 
coast tonight and a chance of coastal showers and isolated storms. 

The main short-term weather hazard will continue to be localized 
flooding rainfall, especially along the coast and inland across 
northeast Florida near and south of the surface front this afternoon 
and into the evening. Rich, deep layer moisture with PWAT near the 
daily max today of 2.3 inches at JAX combined with weak steering 
flow near 5 kts will create slow moving showers and storms, that 
could train near the front and inland from the coast as onshore flow 
develops. 

Leaned on the cooler side of temperatures today given lingering 
clouds and waves of rainfall with highs in the low/mid 80s for 
locations near and east of Interstate 95 and the St. Johns River 
basin to the mid/upper 80s farther inland. Some of the hourly 
guidance is trending about 3-5 deg cooler for many locations today, 
so adjustments may be needed depending on if cloud breaks occur 
later today. Tonight, lows will range in the 70s under elevated NE 
winds along the coast.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY NIGHT/...
Main Highlights This Period:

- Localized Heavy Rain

- Daily Thunderstorms Chances

The cold front over the area shifts towards north central FL on 
Tuesday and will begin to weaken as it sits over central/north 
central FL on Wednesday. Northeasterly onshore flow continues at the 
start of the period as gusty conditions is anticipated along the 
coast, with the stronger winds along SE GA coastal locations and 
local waters. With this flow in place, showers and storms will push 
in from the local waters and towards inland locations from northeast 
to southwest through much of the day. Stronger storms are expected 
to develop over inland locations with peak diurnal heating during 
the afternoon hours. Forecast PWATs sit around the 1.75" to 2" mark 
on Tuesday, so could still some heavy downpours with any shower or 
storm that develop.  

By Wednesday, a more easterly flow develops which will continue to 
push activity in from the Atlantic coast towards inland locations by 
the afternoon hours. Heavy downpours will again be likely as a bit 
more moisture will be aloft from the onshore flow. 

Cooler temperatures on Tuesday behind the front with highs in the 
mid to upper 80s. A bit warmer temperatures on Wednesday as highs 
will be in the upper 80s to lower 90s.

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Main Highlights This Period: 

- Daily Thunderstorms Chances

Chances of precipitation look to steadily decrease through the end 
of the week, with chances of 60% on Thursday trending down to the 
30% to 50% by the weekend. Southerly then southwesterly flow 
develops past midweek and into the upcoming weekend. Guidance 
continues to show another cold front dipping near SE GA on Saturday, 
but may stall north of the area on Sunday. 

Temperatures in the mid 80s to lower 90s during the back half of the 
upcoming week as southwesterly develops heading into this weekend

&&

.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH 06Z TUESDAY/...

Unsettled weather with periods of restrictions as a surface 
front moves across the area this morning and stalls across north 
Florida through tonight. Early this morning fading stratiform rain 
will approach GNV and VQQ from the west the next couple of hours 
with TS activity quickly fading. Winds already shifted to NNE at SSI 
trailing surface front passage, with the wind shift expected at JAX, 
CRG, VQQ and SGJ by 15z then GNV by 18z. Transient ceiling 
restrictions of MVFR to LIFR expected at times this morning as the 
front shifts southward across the terminals and added PROB30 for 
scattered morning showers and isolated storms that will drift inland 
from the coast and also be possible near GNV and VQQ along the 
stalling front. Included TEMPOs this afternoon into the evening 
based on higher TS chances.

&&

.MARINE...

A front stalls across north Florida today then shifts south of the 
waters tonight into Tuesday as high pressure strengthens to the 
northeast. A brief period of Small Craft Exercise Caution conditions 
is possible mainly over the Georgia waters Tuesday as a coastal 
trough develops offshore, then elevated combined seas may bring 
Small Craft Exercise Caution conditions to the outer waters on 
Wednesday as the coastal trough begins weaken. High pressure builds 
east of the local waters Thursday then extends across the Florida 
peninsula Friday into the weekend with a return of westerly winds 
and the afternoon east coast sea breeze.

Rip Currents: Rip current risk increases from north to south
today as onshore flow develops with moderate risk for all local
beaches. By Tuesday, solid moderate to possibly high rip 
current due to stronger and more persistent ENE onshore winds.
High risk likely for all local beaches by Wednesday with
persistent onshore flow and elevated surf with breakers 3-5 ft.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...

- Low Dispersions Over Northeast Florida On Monday

A cold front is expected to shift southward across southeast Georgia 
Today. Low daytime dispersion expected this afternoon across north 
central FL, possibly Tuesday due to more cloudiness and elevated 
rain chances. Surface winds and transport winds will begin to 
transition to northeast to east behind the front Today. Elevated 
rain chances are expected again on Tuesday and Wednesday.  

Fog Potential: Gusty and erratic winds will occur with thunderstorm 
activity. Patchy inland morning fog possible each day.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...

Coastal water levels begin to increase next week with the approach 
of the New Moon on Sept 11th and breezy onshore easterly winds late 
Tonight through Wednesday, with the peak winds across the local 
waters and coast Tuesday. At this time, extended probabilistic 
guidance keeps water levels below action stage late Tuesday through 
Wednesday both along the local Atlantic coast and within the St. 
Johns River basin.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  89  72  87  72 /  60  40  70  20 
SSI  87  77  87  78 /  60  60  60  40 
JAX  89  73  88  74 /  80  50  70  20 
SGJ  87  75  86  76 /  70  40  60  20 
GNV  89  72  88  73 /  70  60  80  20 
OCF  90  73  89  73 /  70  50  80  30 

&&

.JAX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
GA...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
516 AM MDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Better chance for showers and thunderstorms this afternoon with
  locally heavy rain in a few areas across the plains.

- Temperatures will remain very warm, with only slight cool down 
  Tuesday and Wednesday.

- Chance of afternoon thunderstorms mainly Palmer Divide and east
  central plains on Tuesday,

- Warmer and drier for Thursday and Friday.

- Some potential for a brief cooldown next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Sunday/...
Issued at 233 AM MDT Mon Sep 7 2026

A upper level trough will move across the nrn Rockies today thru 
tonight with SW flow aloft across the area. Monsoon moisture will
be embedded in the flow with PW values 150 to 175 percent above 
normal. MLCAPE will be around 1000 j/kg from the Palmer Divide 
across the far ern plains this aftn with lower values further 
west. Overall, will see a good chance of showers/tstms this aftn 
thru the evening hours, especially across the plains. There is 
enough shear for an isold svr storm or two where the highest 
MLCAPE will exist this aftn. In addition, with decent PW's some 
locally heavy rainfall will be possible as well. Highs this aftn 
will be in the upper 80's to mid 90's across the plains.

On Tue, the flow aloft will become more westerly as a wek cool front 
moves across the plains.  There will still be some monsoon moisture 
embedded in the flow, however, PW values will decrease, especially 
across the nrn half of the area.  Best chc for showers/tstms will be 
over the Palmer Divide and sern areas of the plains.  MLCAPE is fcst 
to be in the 500-800 j/kg range, however, shear will be better so 
can't rule out an isold svr storm over the Palmer Divide.  Highs 
across the plains will be in the 85 to 90 degree range.

For Wed, the flow aloft will become more WNW as a surge of cooler 
air moves across late Tue night into Wed morning.  This will lead 
mainly dry conditions with highs across nern CO in the upper 70's to 
mid 80's.

Looking ahead to Thu and Fri, the flow aloft will be mainly zonal 
with minimal moisture embedded in the flow.  As a result, expect 
mainly dry conditions both days with warmer temperatures as readings 
over nern CO rise back into the upper 80's to lower 90s.

For next weekend, the flow aloft will remain zonal on Sat as another 
weak front moves across.  As a result, highs will drop back into the 
80's across the plains.  Meanwhile, will leave in a slight chc for 
aftn tstms across the area.  On Sun, the flow aloft will become more 
SW as an upper level trough moves into the nrn Rockies.  The GFS is 
faster with moving a cold front across the area during the day while 
the ECMWF is slower.  With SW flow aloft and upper level trough 
still to the NW of the area, ECMWF probably has a better handle on 
timing of front.  Thus may see highs reach the upper 80's to lower 
90's over nern CO on Sun before it reaches the area Sun night. 

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS through 12Z Tuesday/...
Issued at 512 AM MDT Mon Sep 7 2026

Winds will become light and variable by 14z and then trend to 
more easterly at BJC and DIA by 17z. At APA, winds will be from 
the SE by 17z and then switch to the NW by 21z. There will be a 
chc of showers/tstms by 22z which will linger thru 02z this evening.
Have kept a prob30 between 22z and 02z for -tsra with brief gusty
winds up to 35 mph possible.  

By 02z, shower/tstm activity should end with winds becoming SE/S 
and then S/SSW by 06z.

&&

.BOU WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$
